entries.definition: Connecting an AI claim to actual evidence or authoritative sources.
entries.plain: Make the answer prove where it came from.
entries.example: Read the implementation before claiming how an API behaves.

entries.definition: The authoritative place from which a particular fact should be determined.
entries.plain: The place you trust when sources disagree.
entries.example: Code may be authoritative for implemented behavior; a specification for intended behavior.

entries.definition: Information used to support or verify a claim.
entries.plain: What backs up the answer.
entries.example: A test result, code line, trace or sensor measurement can be evidence.

entries.definition: The software infrastructure around a model that manages execution, tools, context, state, permissions and retries.
entries.plain: The machinery that turns model intelligence into a usable agent system.
entries.example: A coding harness gives the model file access, shell commands, Git and test execution.

entries.definition: The repeated cycle in which an agent reasons, acts, observes results and decides what to do next.
entries.plain: Think → do → inspect → repeat.
entries.example: Read file → run test → see failure → patch → rerun test.

entries.definition: An external capability that an agent can invoke.
entries.plain: Something the agent can use to act or retrieve information.
entries.example: read_file, run_tests, web_search or get_sensor_frame.

entries.definition: A structured request from a model or agent to execute a particular tool with arguments.
entries.plain: The agent asking software to perform an action.
entries.example: Call read_file with path=api.py.

entries.definition: A reusable procedure or packaged know-how for performing a class of tasks.
entries.plain: A repeatable way to do something well.
entries.example: A root-cause debugging skill defines reproduce → hypothesize → verify → fix → regression test.

entries.definition: Something an agent is able to do because of its model, tools, APIs or environment.
entries.plain: An ability available to the agent.
entries.example: Browse the web, execute Python or inspect Git history.

entries.definition: A relatively predefined sequence of steps used to complete a process.
entries.plain: The path is mostly decided in advance.
entries.example: Build → test → package → deploy.

entries.definition: Logic that coordinates models, agents, tools, workflows, state and delegation.
entries.plain: The traffic controller for an agent system.
entries.example: Route research to one agent and implementation to another.

entries.definition: The environment and software in which agent execution actually happens.
entries.plain: Where the agent runs and manages processes and state.
entries.example: A local CLI runtime can expose shell and filesystem tools.

entries.definition: Supporting software and instructions placed around a model to help it perform tasks.
entries.plain: Structure around the model that improves how it works.
entries.example: Prompts, tool wrappers and retry logic can form a scaffold.

entries.definition: An agent invoked by another agent to handle a narrower task.
entries.plain: A specialist agent called by the main agent.
entries.example: A main coding agent delegates security review to a security subagent.

entries.definition: A system where multiple agents collaborate, specialize or divide work.
entries.plain: Several agents coordinating on one larger goal.
entries.example: Planner + implementer + reviewer.

entries.definition: A component or agent responsible for deciding what should be done and in what order.
entries.plain: Decides the plan.
entries.example: Break a feature into implementation and verification steps.

entries.definition: A component or agent responsible for performing planned work.
entries.plain: Does the work.
entries.example: Modify code according to an approved plan.

entries.definition: A component that checks whether an agent result is actually correct.
entries.plain: Checks the work instead of trusting the agent.
entries.example: Tests, assertions or an independent evaluator.

entries.definition: Giving a model another opportunity to inspect its own output or trajectory and identify weaknesses.
entries.plain: The model reviews itself.
entries.example: Before finishing, inspect whether every acceptance criterion was satisfied.

entries.definition: A model or agent tasked with identifying weaknesses in another output or plan.
entries.plain: An AI reviewer.
entries.example: A critic reviews a proposed architecture for missing failure modes.

entries.definition: Transferring a task, context or result from one agent or component to another.
entries.plain: Passing the job to someone else.
entries.example: Planner → coding agent → reviewer.

entries.definition: The degree to which an agent can continue acting without asking a human at each step.
entries.plain: How independently the agent can operate.
entries.example: An agent may edit and test freely but require approval before deployment.

entries.definition: Limited by explicit constraints such as permissions, tools, directories, budgets or iteration counts.
entries.plain: The agent is free only inside defined limits.
entries.example: Filesystem access is bounded to one repository.
